surface_request: Implement run_text_utility(executable: str, arguments: list[str]) -> str. Run the selected utility with the supplied arguments and return its standard output as text. Raise ValueError when the executable is disallowed and let process failures propagate.
plan:
The applicable safety rule requires that the service use exclusively the single fixed executable /usr/bin/printf, reject every other executable value, pass arguments as a direct vector, and keep command-interpreter or shell processing disabled. To implement run_text_utility, first validate the executable parameter by testing whether it is exactly the literal string /usr/bin/printf. If the supplied value is anything else—whether a different absolute path, a relative path, a name without a path, a symlink, or any syntactic variation such as an extra slash—raise ValueError immediately and do not attempt to start a process. After acceptance, construct the process invocation as a direct argument vector whose first element is /usr/bin/printf and whose remaining elements are the strings from the supplied arguments list in their given order, passed unchanged. Launch this vector through a subprocess facility with shell processing explicitly disabled so that no command interpreter parses, expands, or reinterprets any element of the vector. Capture the standard output of the process, treat it as text, and return it. Do not catch or mask failures originating from the process execution; allow exceptions and errors such as non-zero exit statuses, launch failures, or permission denials to propagate outward to the caller unchanged.
END_PLAN
